intent: Implement parseDuration in src/duration.js (an ES module; keep the export). It takes a string like "1h30m" and returns milliseconds as a number. Units: ms, s, m, h, d. Parts are written largest unit first, each unit at most once, and may be separated by spaces ("1h 30m"). A part's number may have a decimal fraction ("1.5h"). A leading "-" makes the whole duration negative. "0" alone is 0. Anything else (an empty string, a number with no unit, an unknown unit, a unit twice or out of order, a non-string) throws a TypeError. Do not add dependencies. When you are done, say so in one line.
